note: Human test definitions. Do not record a pass without a person performing the test. Guidepup simulation is not a real screen-reader session.

tests.title: Color alone is not used to convey meaning
tests.purpose: Confirm that a person can tell which kind of message this is without seeing the variant color or icon.
tests.preconditions: Open each alert variant. Hide or ignore color, for example with a grayscale filter or by reading the text only.
steps: Open the informational, success, warning, error, and emergency states.
Read only the heading and body text.
Decide whether the meaning is still clear.
Repeat without the colored border and icon visible.
tests.expected: The heading and text communicate the message type and urgency without relying on color, icon shape, or position alone.
tests.notes: The baseline may pass this check while the experimental theme changes border and background colors. Record which pane you tested.

tests.title: Alert text and boundaries meet contrast requirements
tests.purpose: Measure the rendered text against its background and the alert boundary against the page.
tests.preconditions: Use a contrast analyzer or the browser developer tools on the rendered page. Record the tool and metric.
steps: Measure heading and body text against the alert background in light mode.
Repeat in dark mode if the experimental theme supports it.
Measure the alert boundary and icon against the adjacent background.
Record the measured ratios, not a pass/fail estimate.
tests.expected: Body text reaches at least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1 under WCAG 2.x. Non-text boundaries reach 3:1 where they carry meaning.
tests.notes: WCAG 2.x ratios and APCA scores are different metrics. State which one was used; do not compare them as equivalent.

tests.title: Alert headings and labels are clear and descriptive
tests.purpose: Check that a heading announces the consequence, not only the severity word.
tests.preconditions: Read the alert in page context.
steps: Read each heading without the body text.
Ask whether the heading describes the problem or outcome.
Check that the heading level fits the surrounding page outline.
tests.expected: Each heading is understandable on its own and does not mislead about the outcome.
tests.notes: Heading quality depends on the implementation's content and cannot be decided by an automated scanner.

tests.title: Each alert variant has a consistent meaning across the site
tests.purpose: Confirm that the same visual and semantic treatment is not reused for a different meaning elsewhere.
tests.preconditions: Review more than one page that uses alerts.
steps: Compare the warning, error, and success treatments across pages.
Check that no other element copies the same icon, color, and heading pattern for a different purpose.
Record any reuse that changes the meaning.
tests.expected: A warning always reads as a warning, and the treatment is not reused for unrelated content.
tests.notes: This test needs the wider implementation, not the single lab fixture.

tests.title: Alert remains readable and functional at 400% zoom
tests.purpose: Check that zooming does not clip the alert or push controls out of the viewport.
tests.preconditions: Use real browser zoom at 400% in a 1280 CSS-pixel viewport, or the equivalent 320 CSS-pixel layout.
steps: Zoom the browser to 400%.
Read the full alert and any links in it.
Check that no content requires two-dimensional scrolling.
Record the browser, operating system, and actual zoom level.
tests.expected: The alert wraps and remains readable without horizontal scrolling, clipped text, or lost controls.
tests.notes: A CSS text-size change is not browser zoom. Do not mark this passed from the lab's text-size control alone.

tests.title: Content survives the WCAG text-spacing overrides
tests.purpose: Check that increased line, paragraph, letter, and word spacing does not clip or overlap the alert.
tests.preconditions: Apply the WCAG 1.4.12 values: line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em.
steps: Open the alert with the spacing preset or a user stylesheet.
Read every line and link.
Check for clipping, overlap, and hidden controls.
Repeat with long content and a narrow viewport.
tests.expected: All text remains visible and usable; no content overlaps or is cut off.
tests.notes: The lab's spacing preset applies these values. Record that this is a CSS override, not a user stylesheet.

tests.title: Screen reader reads the alert in a logical order
tests.purpose: Check that the announced order matches the visual and logical reading order.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader: NVDA, JAWS, or VoiceOver.
steps: Navigate to the alert with the screen reader's reading commands.
Listen to the heading, body, and any link.
Compare the spoken order with the visual order.
tests.expected: The heading is announced before its explanatory text, and links are announced in context.
tests.notes: Guidepup transcripts can help investigate but do not count as this test.

tests.title: Screen reader communicates the alert region or role
tests.requirement: WCAG 1.3.6 Identify Purpose, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
tests.purpose: Check what role, if any, is announced for static and status alerts.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader.
steps: Navigate to a static informational alert.
Record whether a region, status, alert, or no role is announced.
Repeat for an error alert.
Confirm that a decorative wrapper is not announced as a landmark.
tests.expected: The announced role matches the intended behaviour: static content is not falsely announced as an urgent alert, and status changes use an appropriate live role.
tests.notes: Do not add role=alert to content that is already present on page load.

tests.title: Role values are announced for time-sensitive alerts
tests.purpose: Check whether an alert that must interrupt is exposed with role=alert, and whether the interruption is justified.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Trigger the alert yourself.
steps: Trigger the dynamic or urgent alert.
Listen for the announcement and the role.
Decide whether interrupting the user was necessary.
Record the exact spoken output.
tests.expected: The role is announced and the level of interruption matches the urgency. Non-urgent messages do not use role=alert.
tests.notes: Assertive live regions can interrupt. Use them only for urgent changes.

tests.title: Status alerts are announced without moving focus
tests.purpose: Confirm that a status message is announced politely and focus stays where the person left it.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Place focus on the button that triggers the message.
steps: Activate the button that inserts the status alert.
Listen for the announcement.
Check where focus is after the announcement.
Repeat with a second update.
tests.expected: The status is announced without stealing focus, and the updated text is announced when it changes.
tests.notes: This is a human test. The virtual screen reader transcript is supporting evidence only.

tests.title: A newly inserted alert is understandable and not unnecessarily disruptive
tests.purpose: Determine whether a newly displayed alert is announced appropriately.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Start with the alert absent.
steps: Open the fixture using a real screen reader.
Navigate to the trigger control.
Trigger the action that causes the alert to appear.
Listen to the announcement.
Determine whether the message is understandable.
Check whether existing speech is unnecessarily interrupted.
Record the result.
tests.expected: The announcement communicates the intended message without unnecessary interruption, and the person can continue the task.
tests.notes: Record the screen reader, browser, operating system, and exact announcement.

tests.title: Accordion buttons toggle with Enter and Space and keep focus
tests.purpose: Confirm that each disclosure is a native button and that keyboard activation changes state without moving focus.
tests.preconditions: Open the accordion fixture in a real browser. Start with both panels closed.
steps: Tab to the first disclosure button.
Press Enter; check that the panel opens and focus stays on the button.
Press Space; check that it closes and focus stays.
Repeat for the second button and record the exact state change.
tests.expected: Enter and Space both toggle the panel, aria-expanded follows, and focus remains on the control.
tests.notes: The automated keyboard test covers this in Chromium; a person still needs to confirm the experience.

tests.title: Expanded state is exposed and matches the visible panel
tests.purpose: Check that assistive technology receives the same expanded/collapsed state a sighted person sees.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader or inspect the accessibility tree while opening and closing each panel.
steps: Open the first panel.
Read the button state and count how many panels are visible.
Close it and repeat.
Repeat with both panels open.
tests.expected: The announced expanded state and the number of visible panels agree in every state.
tests.notes: Guidepup transcripts support investigation but do not count as this human test.

tests.title: Screen reader reads heading, button, and panel in logical order
tests.purpose: Check that the heading text and the disclosure control are announced in an order that makes sense.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Open the fixture and move through it with reading commands.
steps: Read the page heading and the first accordion heading.
Activate the button and read into the panel.
Continue to the second heading and panel.
Record any duplicated or skipped heading.
tests.expected: Each heading precedes its button, panel content follows the button, and no content is announced twice or skipped.
tests.notes: A DOM snapshot can suggest a problem but not prove the spoken order.

tests.title: Accordion content survives large text, text spacing, and a narrow width
tests.purpose: Check that long panel content and the control label do not clip or overlap when space is constrained.
tests.preconditions: Use the 320 CSS-px width, 200% text, and the WCAG text-spacing preset, then optionally real browser zoom.
steps: Open both panels.
Set 320 px width and 200% text.
Apply the text-spacing preset.
Read the long panel and the link to the end.
tests.expected: Text wraps, the link remains reachable, and no control or content is cut off or overlapped.
tests.notes: CSS scaling is not browser zoom; record which condition was used.

tests.title: Accordion content remains readable when JavaScript is unavailable
tests.requirement: Progressive enhancement / WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
tests.purpose: Confirm that hiding content behind a dead control is not the only no-script experience.
tests.preconditions: Disable JavaScript in the browser and open the accordion fixture.
steps: Open the fixture with JavaScript disabled.
Check that panel content is visible.
Check that no visible button claims a collapsed state without working.
Read the long panel.
tests.expected: The content is readable and no dead disclosure control is presented.
tests.notes: The lab fixture stylesheet expands hidden panels and hides dead buttons without JavaScript.

tests.title: Banner disclosure is keyboard operable and keeps its name
tests.requirement: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.4 Link Purpose, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
tests.purpose: Check that the banner can be expanded without a mouse and that the control has an understandable name.
tests.preconditions: Open the banner fixture in a real browser. Start collapsed.
steps: Tab to the banner disclosure button.
Press Enter; confirm the panel opens and focus stays.
Press Space; confirm it closes.
Read the accessible name of the button.
tests.expected: The control is a native button with a meaningful name, toggles with Enter and Space, and keeps focus.
tests.notes: The automated test covers Chromium; a person still confirms the experience.

tests.title: Banner communicates service identity without color or icon
tests.requirement: WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
tests.purpose: Check that the banner text explains the site identity without relying on the flag icon or color.
tests.preconditions: View the banner with color ignored and read only the text.
steps: Read the banner prompt and the action label.
Open the panel and read both headings and bodies.
Check whether the text alone says what the banner is for.
Repeat without the icon visible.
tests.expected: The text explains the service identity and the purpose of the disclosure; color and icon are supplementary.
tests.notes: Banner content is implementation-specific; this lab uses neutral demonstration text.

tests.title: Expanded banner content is readable in a logical order
tests.purpose: Check that the two explanatory panels are reachable and ordered as presented.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Expand the banner.
steps: Expand the banner with the keyboard.
Read the panel headings and bodies in order.
Check that no focus is stolen after expansion.
Record the exact announcement.
tests.expected: Both panels are announced in the visual order, focus stays on the trigger, and the expansion is not announced as an urgent alert.
tests.notes: A banner disclosure is not a live status message.

tests.title: Banner text and focus indicator meet contrast requirements
tests.requirement: WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, 2.4.7 Focus Visible
tests.purpose: Measure the banner text, the action label, and the keyboard focus indicator on the rendered surface.
tests.preconditions: Use a contrast analyzer and the keyboard. Record the tool and the WCAG metric.
steps: Measure the prompt and action text against the banner background.
Measure the expanded panel text.
Focus the disclosure button and measure the indicator against its adjacent colors.
Repeat in dark and forced-colours emulation where available.
tests.expected: Body text reaches at least 4.5:1, large text at least 3:1, and the focus indicator is clearly distinguishable.
tests.notes: Forced colours and dark mode are captured by browser emulation, not a real high-contrast device.

tests.title: Banner content is reachable when JavaScript is unavailable
tests.requirement: Progressive enhancement / WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
tests.purpose: Confirm that the banner does not hide its only explanation behind a dead disclosure control.
tests.preconditions: Disable JavaScript in the browser and open the banner fixture.
steps: Open the fixture with JavaScript disabled.
Check that the banner panels are visible.
Check that no dead banner button is presented.
Read both panel headings.
tests.expected: The banner content is readable without JavaScript and no non-working disclosure control is shown.
tests.notes: The fixture stylesheet handles this fallback; production implementations must do the same.

tests.title: Every control has a visible label, hint, and group name
tests.requirement: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
tests.purpose: Check that a person can identify each control and the required radio group without guessing from placeholder text.
tests.preconditions: Open the form fixture. Do not submit it yet.
steps: Read each visible label and hint.
Check the radio group legend and each option label.
Check that required status is stated in text, not only color.
Compare the accessible name of each control with its visible label.
tests.expected: Every control has a visible, meaningful label; hints are associated; the group has a legend; required status is in text.
tests.notes: Automated name checks can confirm an association but not whether the wording is clear.

tests.title: Invalid submission identifies the problem and moves focus
tests.requirement: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion, 2.4.3 Focus Order
tests.purpose: Check the native validation experience when required fields are empty.
tests.preconditions: Open the form in the empty state. Use a browser that shows native validation messages.
steps: Submit the empty form.
Observe which control receives focus.
Read the browser error message.
Correct the fields one at a time and resubmit.
tests.expected: The first invalid control receives focus, the message identifies the problem in plain language, and correcting the values allows submission.
tests.notes: Native messages are browser-controlled; record the browser and OS.

tests.title: Screen reader communicates the invalid field and error guidance
tests.requirement: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
tests.purpose: Determine what a screen-reader user hears after an empty submit and whether the error is discoverable.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Open the form empty.
steps: Submit the form with the keyboard.
Record the spoken message and focus location.
Navigate back to the radio group and text input.
Correct the fields and submit again.
tests.expected: The error and the affected controls are announced understandably, focus moves predictably, and the successful result is announced.
tests.notes: Native validation speech differs by browser and screen reader; record both.

tests.title: Valid submission shows a status without sending data
tests.purpose: Check that a successful local submission is announced and that nothing is sent over the network.
tests.preconditions: Open the form. Use the browser network panel or an offline connection.
steps: Complete the required radio and reference field.
Submit the form.
Listen for the status announcement.
Check the network panel for requests.
tests.expected: A local status message is visible and announced, and no network request carries the entered data.
tests.notes: The fixture is local-only by design; production forms need separate privacy testing.

tests.title: Native validation still works without JavaScript
tests.purpose: Check that the form does not depend on the lab script to block invalid submission.
tests.preconditions: Disable JavaScript and open the form fixture.
steps: Submit the empty form.
Observe the native validation message and focus.
Complete the required fields.
Submit again and check that no data is sent.
tests.expected: Native constraint validation still blocks invalid submission and permits valid submission without JavaScript.
tests.notes: The fixture uses native required attributes; no custom error script is needed.

tests.title: Radio group has a legend and each option has a label
tests.requirement: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
tests.purpose: Check that the question and the options are announced as one group.
tests.preconditions: Open the radio-validation fixture read-only.
steps: Read the group legend.
Read each option label.
Check that the options share one group name.
Compare the accessible names with the visible text.
tests.expected: The legend names the question, each option has a distinct label, and the group is announced together.
tests.notes: A visual group without a fieldset/legend may look correct but be ambiguous to a screen reader.

tests.title: Radio group is one tab stop and arrow keys change selection
tests.purpose: Confirm native radio keyboard behavior is preserved.
tests.preconditions: Open the fixture. Clear any selection.
steps: Tab into the group and count the tab stops.
Press Arrow Down and Arrow Up.
Press Space on the focused option.
Tab out of the group.
tests.expected: The group is one tab stop, arrows move and select within the group, Space selects, and Tab leaves the group.
tests.notes: Do not add custom arrow-key handlers on top of native radios.

tests.title: Empty required radio submission is blocked with a clear message
tests.requirement: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion, 2.4.3 Focus Order
tests.purpose: Check native required-group validation and focus placement.
tests.preconditions: Open the fixture with no option selected.
steps: Submit the form.
Observe focus and the native message.
Select an option and submit again.
Record the exact message and focus target.
tests.expected: Submission is blocked, the first radio or group receives focus, the message explains the required choice, and selecting an option allows submission.
tests.notes: The native message is browser-controlled; record the browser and OS.

tests.title: Valid radio submission shows a local status
tests.purpose: Check that a successful local choice is announced without moving focus unexpectedly.
tests.preconditions: Open the fixture. Select one option.
steps: Submit the form with the keyboard.
Listen for the status message.
Check the focus location.
Check the network panel for requests.
tests.expected: A local confirmation is announced politely, focus remains predictable, and nothing is sent.
tests.notes: The status region is outside the radio group and uses role=status.

tests.title: Required radio validation works without JavaScript
tests.purpose: Confirm the required group does not depend on the lab script.
tests.preconditions: Disable JavaScript and open the radio fixture.
steps: Submit without a selection.
Observe the native message and focus.
Select an option and submit.
Check that no data is sent.
tests.expected: Native required validation blocks the empty submission and permits the selected submission without JavaScript.
tests.notes: The reset button and status are script-assisted; the native constraint remains the fallback.
